title: L01 — Leadership commitment and accountable safety roles
purpose: Make safety decisions owned and resourced across dispersed crews.
practicalBoundary: Explain responsibilities and escalation; supervisor scenario discussion. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: L02 — Worker participation and safety meetings
purpose: Surface changing field hazards through worker input.
practicalBoundary: Raise a concern, contribute to risk review, confirm understanding; facilitated exercise. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: L03 — Stop-work and safe restart
purpose: Give every worker authority to interrupt uncontrolled energy exposure.
practicalBoundary: Practice intervention and escalation; scenario and supervisor observation. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: L04 — Subcontractor selection and safety bridging
purpose: Prevent lower-tier gaps between service scope and client controls.
practicalBoundary: Identify conflicting rules and responsibility boundaries; bridging case exercise. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: L05 — Service applicability, legal obligations and controlled documents
purpose: Keep each Vendor assessed against actual work and current procedures.
practicalBoundary: Recognize when scope changes need reassessment; document-version exercise. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: H01 — Task risk assessment and JSA/JHA
purpose: Identify energy sources and effective controls before routine and nonroutine work.
practicalBoundary: A suitable assessor must observe the learner analyze an actual or safely simulated task, identify harm pathways and affected people, select controls within role limits, verify assigned safeguards, brief a worker and respond to a change. Technical isolations, lifting, gas testing and other specialist work require their own qualified practical evaluations and authorization. A written JSA exercise does not qualify the learner to execute those hazardous tasks.

title: H02 — Critical-control checks and line of fire
purpose: Prevent crushing, struck-by and stored-energy harm.
practicalBoundary: A competent assessor must separately observe identification of actual energy paths, safe positioning, establishment and verification of assigned boundaries, agreed stop signals and response to a failed critical control. Specialized isolation, rigging, operating, pressure-system and restraint decisions require their own qualifications and practical authorization. This course does not qualify a worker to calculate exclusion zones, design restraints or direct hazardous equipment movement.

title: H03 — Permit to work and SIMOPS coordination — Training
purpose: Coordinate simultaneous work near operating hydrocarbon systems.
practicalBoundary: Separate task-specific practical evaluation and employer/site authorization are required.

title: H04 — Hazardous energy isolation / LOTO
purpose: Control unexpected startup and residual energy.
practicalBoundary: Authorized isolation personnel require equipment-specific instruction and a practical evaluation of source identification, device application, stored-energy control, verification, group participation, handover and restoration. Electrical testing and process isolation may require additional specialist qualifications. Affected workers need practical instruction in respecting restrictions and communicating changes. This written course grants no device-removal, test or restoration authority.

title: H05 — Confined-space entry
purpose: Control atmosphere, engulfment, access and rescue risks.
practicalBoundary: A qualified assessor must separately evaluate each assigned entry role using the actual program and a safe representative space or simulation: hazard recognition, equipment, communications, monitoring duties, exit actions and accountability. Gas testing requires instrument and sampling competence. Rescue requires a separately qualified and equipped service with appropriate practice. This course neither authorizes entry nor replaces jurisdiction-specific entry training.

title: H06 — Hot work and fire watch
purpose: Prevent fire/explosion during work around flammable materials.
practicalBoundary: Separately assess the assigned hot-work craft skill, fire-watch duties, extinguisher and emergency actions, area preparation and permit acceptance in safe practical exercises. Gas testing and permit issuing require their own qualified evaluation and designation. This course is not a welding qualification, gas-testing certificate or authorization to fight fires beyond assigned safe limits.

title: H07 — Lifting, rigging and suspended loads
purpose: Avoid dropped loads, overturning and line-of-fire exposure.
practicalBoundary: Operators, riggers, signal persons, lifting leads and planners require separately assessed task-specific competence and any applicable certification or licensing. Practical assessment must address the actual equipment, load information, rigging, signals, exclusion, deviations and landing. This awareness course does not authorize calculations, rigging selection or crane operation.

title: H08 — Work at height, scaffolds and dropped objects
purpose: Prevent falls and falling-object injuries.
practicalBoundary: Qualified assessors must separately evaluate the assigned access equipment, harness fitting and connections, movement, inspection, tool control and emergency actions. Scaffold erection, alteration and inspection, anchorage design and rescue require their own competent or qualified roles. This course does not grant scaffold, lift, rope-access or rescue authority.

title: H09 — Excavation and underground services
purpose: Prevent utility strikes, collapse and hazardous access.
practicalBoundary: A designated competent person must separately demonstrate excavation inspection and hazard recognition within the applicable requirements. Soil classification, protective-system selection or design, utility locating and exposure, plant operation and rescue require their own qualified practical capabilities. This awareness course authorizes none of those specialist functions.

title: H10 — Pressure pumping, testing and exclusion zones
purpose: Prevent high-energy release and incompatible pressure equipment use.
practicalBoundary: Pressure-system designers, test leaders and operators require separate technical qualification and practical evaluation of the actual system, limits, setup, instrumentation, exclusion, shutdown and verified depressurization. This course does not authorize test-pressure selection, assembly approval or hands-on testing.

title: H11 — Breaking containment and process handback
purpose: Prevent hydrocarbon/chemical release on opening equipment.
practicalBoundary: Separately assess equipment identification, process preparation, isolation coordination, verified safe state, approved opening method, exposure protection, stop response and reinstatement for the actual role. Technical isolation, gas testing and process integrity acceptance require their own qualified personnel. This written course does not authorize line opening or operating restoration.

title: H12 — Electrical work and arc-flash controls
purpose: Prevent shock, arc flash and ignition.
practicalBoundary: Qualified electrical personnel require separate practical evaluation for the equipment and tasks, including source identification, isolation, suitable testing, protective systems, boundaries and restoration. Licensing and employer designation apply where required. Electrical rescue and first aid are separately trained capabilities. This course does not authorize opening panels, testing voltage or energized repair.

title: H13 — H2S and hazardous-atmosphere awareness
purpose: Recognize gas danger and escape without unplanned rescue.
practicalBoundary: A qualified H2S instructor or other suitable specialist must separately assess the actual assigned detection, alarm recognition, escape equipment, route selection, communication and accountability actions in safe practical exercises. Field gas testing additionally requires instrument-specific training, sampling and interpretation competence, documented practical evaluation and employer/site authorization. Respirator use requires the applicable respiratory program prerequisites, including medical evaluation and fit testing where required. Atmospheric rescue is a separate specialist capability; this awareness course neither trains nor authorizes entry rescue.

title: H14 — Chemicals, SDS and exposure assessment
purpose: Make process chemicals, fuels, cleaners and waste hazards visible.
practicalBoundary: Separate practical evaluation must verify SDS access, product/label matching and the assigned handling controls. Exposure assessment, respiratory selection, hazardous-material emergency response and medical decisions require competent specialists and applicable authorizations.

title: H15 — Respiratory protection
purpose: Ensure respiratory equipment matches exposure and user.
practicalBoundary: Separate program administration, medical evaluation, equipment-specific fit testing and safe practical demonstration are required as applicable. This online awareness course does not qualify respirator selection, fit-test administration, supplied-air technical work, emergency entry or rescue.

title: H16 — Silica, asbestos, lead and coating hazards
purpose: Control chronic exposure and contaminated materials.
practicalBoundary: Separate competent material surveys, sampling, exposure assessment, specialist licensing/training, respiratory-program prerequisites and applicable clearance are required. This awareness course authorizes no asbestos abatement, lead removal, hazardous sampling or technical handback.

title: H17 — Noise and hearing conservation
purpose: Prevent cumulative hearing loss in shops and field operations.
practicalBoundary: Competent noise assessment, hearing-protection selection and practical fit/use instruction remain separate. Applicable audiometric surveillance and clinical interpretation belong to qualified health services. Online completion is not a noise survey, fit verification or medical clearance.

title: H18 — Heat, cold and severe weather
purpose: Protect outdoor crews, gate workers and hot-process staff.
practicalBoundary: Practical evaluation must verify relief, monitoring, alarms and safe shelter access without deliberate thermal exposure. Medical assessment, first aid and emergency treatment require appropriately trained responders. The employer must establish applicable local controls; this course supplies no universal heat index, work/rest ratio, lightning radius or medical clearance.

title: H19 — Driving, journey planning and fatigue
purpose: Manage remote roads, long shifts and vehicle travel.
practicalBoundary: Separate licence verification, vehicle-specific practical driving assessment, load and equipment competence and applicable legal authorization remain necessary. This online course does not qualify driving, towing, dangerous-goods transport or emergency response.

title: H20 — Traffic, gate access and pedestrian separation
purpose: Prevent vehicle/pedestrian conflict and unsafe admission.
practicalBoundary: Separate site-specific practical evaluation must verify gate positioning, communication, access checks, pedestrian protection, handover and escalation. Spotter, traffic-control and equipment-operation duties require their own applicable training, assessment and authorization. This course does not qualify a worker to direct public-road traffic or conduct security enforcement.

title: H21 — Lone work, workplace violence and remote check-ins
purpose: Ensure help reaches isolated workers and threatening encounters are escalated.
practicalBoundary: A separate practical evaluation must verify task limits, check-in and receiver handover, end-to-end alarms, safe withdrawal and missed-contact escalation in a safe simulation. Security enforcement, rescue, medical response and hazardous-area device approval require their own qualified authorities. This course does not qualify a worker to physically restrain people, enter hazards for rescue or approve lone technical work.

title: H22 — Manual handling and ergonomics
purpose: Reduce strain during handling, repetitive work and prolonged gate/vehicle shifts.
practicalBoundary: A separate safe practical evaluation must verify the selected aid, route, placement and any team coordination. Powered handling equipment needs its own operator authorization. Medical assessment and complex ergonomic evaluation require the appropriate professionals; this course establishes no universal safe load.

title: H23 — Machine guarding, hand tools and housekeeping
purpose: Prevent entanglement, cuts, trips and unsafe temporary arrangements.
practicalBoundary: Separate equipment-specific practical assessment, operator authorization, isolation competence and competent technical maintenance are required as applicable. This course does not authorize bypasses, energized troubleshooting or machine repair.

title: H24 — Specialist hazards: radiation, explosives, diving, marine and rail
purpose: Avoid omitting low-frequency, high-consequence specialist work.
practicalBoundary: This is general specialist-interface AWARENESS only. Radiation work/source recovery, explosives handling/misfire response, commercial diving/rescue, marine operation/transfers and rail access/movement each require their own qualified authority, applicable licences, technical plan, practical assessment and employer/site permission. None is conferred by this course.

title: C01 — Role/task competence matrix and authorization
purpose: Tie capability to the actual tasks each worker may perform.
practicalBoundary: Supervisors map tasks to evidence and recognize expired/out-of-scope credentials. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: C02 — Induction, orientation and understandable communication
purpose: Ensure workers understand hazards, reporting and emergency arrangements.
practicalBoundary: Explain stop work, reporting and emergency actions in understood language; comprehension check. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: C03 — Short-service workers and supervision
purpose: Control unfamiliarity with high-energy tasks and local conditions.
practicalBoundary: Mentors demonstrate coaching and task observation; worker practical assessment. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: C04 — Training delivery and practical assessor assurance
purpose: Prevent attendance certificates from being mistaken for competence.
practicalBoundary: Assessors distinguish knowledge from performance; calibrate using a sample assessment. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: C05 — Commercial drivers and transport authorization
purpose: Keep driver/legal qualification distinct from general awareness.
practicalBoundary: Licensed training/testing and on-road evaluation for vehicle/task; jurisdiction review required. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: C06 — Mobile equipment, forklift and lifting-role assessment
purpose: Match authorization to equipment and work environment.
practicalBoundary: Qualified practical evaluation; forklift rule requires suitable evaluator, not reading or generic card alone. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: C07 — Permit, isolation, gas-test and electrical role endorsements
purpose: Ensure the person signing a control has relevant assessed authority.
practicalBoundary: Role-specific observed task and emergency/abnormal scenario assessment by qualified personnel. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: C08 — Emergency responders and occupational first aid
purpose: Ensure response promises correspond to capable people.
practicalBoundary: Recognized first-aid/CPR provider and practical response/rescue assessment as applicable. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: E01 — Asset register and preventive maintenance
purpose: Maintain traceable safety-critical equipment across fleets and shops.
practicalBoundary: Maintenance personnel and technical release owners require separately assessed competence for the actual equipment and work. Practical evaluation should cover identity, maintenance method, measurements, safety-function testing, defects and release restrictions. Users need equipment-specific pre-use instruction. This course does not qualify repair, statutory examination or engineering certification.

title: E02 — Pre-use inspections, defects and out-of-service control
purpose: Prevent known defects from returning to work uncorrected.
practicalBoundary: A competent assessor must observe pre-use inspection of the actual equipment class, accurate defect reporting, assigned quarantine and correct escalation. Repair, hazardous isolation, technical testing and release require separate task-specific competence and authorization. This written course does not certify equipment condition or authorize specialist repair.

title: E03 — Vehicles, trailers, load securement and recovery
purpose: Control vehicle condition, shifting loads and unsafe recovery.
practicalBoundary: Drivers require the applicable license and observed competence for the actual vehicle and trailer. Loading and securement require task-specific practical instruction and verification; specialist loads need competent planning. Recovery operators need separate assessed capability and suitable equipment. This course does not authorize commercial driving or recovery.

title: E04 — Gas detectors and measurement assurance
purpose: Avoid relying on unserviceable or unsuitable gas instruments.
practicalBoundary: Gas testers require instrument- and task-specific practical assessment of selection, checks, safe sampling, timing, limitations, interpretation, logging and emergency response, plus employer/site authorization. Calibration and repair require the appropriate competent service role. This course does not qualify confined-space clearance, hazardous entry, respiratory use or rescue.

title: E05 — Pressure equipment, hoses and relief devices
purpose: Match components and protection to actual pressure service.
practicalBoundary: Pressure-equipment inspection, statutory examination, hose assembly, relief-device servicing, testing and technical release require separately assessed specialist competence and any applicable certification. Users need practical pre-use and defect-control instruction for their equipment. This course does not approve pressure designs or authorize hazardous testing.

title: E06 — Lifting gear, access equipment and fall protection inspection
purpose: Ensure critical load-bearing equipment is fit and traceable.
practicalBoundary: Practical assessment must match the role: user pre-use checks, competent examination, rigging, scaffold erection or inspection, and fall-protection use or design are distinct capabilities. Qualified assessors must observe the actual equipment class and method. This course does not grant lifting, scaffold, anchorage design or rescue authority.

title: E07 — PPE assessment, issue and care
purpose: Make protection fit the exposure and worker.
practicalBoundary: A competent assessor must observe correct selection understanding, fitting, adjustment, combined-equipment compatibility, inspection, use, removal, care and replacement for the assigned PPE. Respiratory, electrical, hearing, fall-protection and other specialist programs retain their own technical and practical requirements. This course does not grant hazardous-task authorization or replace a fit test.

title: E08 — Shop and facility readiness
purpose: Control fixed machinery, storage and emergency access between jobs.
practicalBoundary: General inspection awareness does not replace electrical, fire-system, pressure-system, racking or machinery technical examination. Separate competent assessors must verify relevant systems and practical facility actions. This course authorizes no technical repair or certification.

title: E09 — Vacuum, hydroblasting and specialist service equipment
purpose: Prevent static ignition, suction and high-pressure injury.
practicalBoundary: Separate equipment-specific technical training, supervised practical evaluation and employer/site authorization are required for vacuum and hydroblasting operators. Specialist approval must set ratings, compatibility, atmospheric and ignition controls, isolation and emergency arrangements. This awareness course supplies no operating parameters and authorizes no confined-space entry or equipment intervention.

title: I01 — Incident, near-miss and hazard reporting
purpose: Enable timely learning without hiding events or rewarding report volume.
practicalBoundary: Distinguish hazard/near miss/incident; scenario-based reporting and emergency escalation. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: I02 — Investigation and causal analysis
purpose: Find failed controls and organizational causes rather than blame alone.
practicalBoundary: Qualified investigator instruction and assessed case analysis; complex events need specialist investigators. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: I03 — Corrective actions and effectiveness verification
purpose: Distinguish completing a task from fixing a safety weakness.
practicalBoundary: Develop control-focused actions and test recurrence/implementation; assessed case. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: I04 — Learning alerts and post-job review
purpose: Transfer learning between crews and repeat work.
practicalBoundary: Extract actionable learning and explain change; facilitated debrief. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: I05 — Incident history and exposure-data integrity
purpose: Keep transparent event context without treating zero reports as maturity.
practicalBoundary: Reconcile denominators and distinguish unknown from verified zero; data exercise. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: I06 — Medical response, restricted records and return-to-work interfaces
purpose: Coordinate care and safe restrictions while protecting worker privacy.
practicalBoundary: Supervisors act within role and protect health information; clinical decisions require clinicians. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

title: R01 — Emergency plan and site interface
purpose: Ensure credible response for remote sites and hazardous operations.
practicalBoundary: Separate site orientation and safe practical demonstration must verify alarm recognition, evacuation/shelter, accountability, reporting and responder access. Technical shutdown, firefighting, rescue and medical response require their own trained roles and authorization.

title: R02 — Rescue plans and emergency equipment readiness
purpose: Avoid relying on unavailable rescue or unplanned entry.
practicalBoundary: Qualified rescue authorities must separately approve methods, verify response capability and conduct safe technical practical evaluations. This course qualifies no confined-space, rope, fall, diving, water or medical rescuer and supplies no universal rescue response-time threshold.

title: R03 — Drills, exercises and after-action improvement
purpose: Test whether plans and people work together under credible conditions.
practicalBoundary: Separate qualified oversight is needed for technical rescue and equipment exercises. Practical emergency capability must be observed safely within the actual scope. This course qualifies no rescuer and authorizes no live exposure, hazardous drill condition or universal readiness certification.

title: R04 — Assurance audits and critical-control observations
purpose: Check actual implementation beyond document existence.
practicalBoundary: Technical assurance requires reviewers competent in the relevant subject and safe authorized observation. This course does not qualify technical certification, regulatory inspection, rescue approval or operating permission. Company review remains separate from site readiness.

title: R05 — Management review and improvement objectives
purpose: Make leadership respond to recurring gaps and changing work.
practicalBoundary: Separate leadership review of actual evidence and resources is required; online completion is not an audit opinion or proof of company effectiveness. Technical controls and operational restart remain with qualified specialists and responsible employer/site authorities.

title: R06 — Management of change and renewal review
purpose: Reassess controls when services, people, assets or procedures change.
practicalBoundary: Separate qualified technical review, applicable practical equipment assessment and employer/site startup authorization remain required. This course does not authorize protective-system bypasses, engineering design or expired work. No universal change or renewal period is established.

title: R07 — Environmental release and spill emergency interface
purpose: Coordinate personnel safety, containment and external response.
practicalBoundary: Separate hazardous-material response training, atmospheric assessment, source isolation, medical care, environmental notification decisions, waste management and technical handback require the appropriate qualified roles. This course authorizes no entry into unknown atmospheres or specialist spill cleanup and defines no universal reporting threshold.

title: G01 — Hazardous-material transportation: recognition and safe handoff
purpose: Close the transport-recognition teaching gap while preserving separate function-specific, mode-specific and practical qualification requirements.
practicalBoundary: This foundation is not a complete PHMSA, dangerous-goods, HAZWOPER or all-mode qualification. Employer function/material/mode instruction, testing, certification and any practical evaluation remain separate requirements.

title: G02 — Hazardous waste and spill response: role limits and safe handoffs
purpose: Teach workers to recognize and escalate hazardous-waste/response training gaps without claiming specialist capability.
practicalBoundary: This foundation is not a HAZWOPER initial, refresher, responder-level or supervised-field-experience program. Appropriate employer-specific instruction, time-based requirements, medical arrangements and qualified practical evaluations remain separate.

title: G03 — Process safety and operating-procedure competence
purpose: Recognize loss-of-control pathways and support disciplined procedure, safeguard, change and handback decisions.
practicalBoundary: Foundation knowledge does not qualify plant operation, safeguard testing, bypasses, process changes or restart. Actual process information, procedures, assessment and employer/site authority remain separate.

title: G04 — Bloodborne pathogens and occupational exposure controls
purpose: Prevent occupational contact with human blood and other potentially infectious material and support prompt confidential response when exposure may occur.
practicalBoundary: Written completion does not establish clinical qualification, cleanup or sharps-handling competence, employer-specific exposure-control implementation, interactive Q&A, vaccination or confidential medical follow-up. Those require the appropriate employer, assessor and clinical processes.

title: G05 — Food hygiene, allergens and catering controls
purpose: Prevent foodborne illness and allergen exposure through understood hygiene, actual measured process control and reliable receiving-to-service handoff.
practicalBoundary: Knowledge completion does not supply a food-handler/manager credential, health permit, clinical clearance, approved process, allergen-free guarantee or observed practical competence. Local adoption, product/process SOPs and employer-specific assessment remain separate.

title: G06 — Laboratory chemical hygiene and analytical task safety
purpose: Connect sample and method hazards with effective chemical hygiene, equipment, waste and emergency controls.
practicalBoundary: Knowledge completion does not validate a method, implement a chemical hygiene plan or qualify specialized analytical, biological, radiation, medical or instrument-repair work. Method-specific instruction, assessment and authorization remain separate.

title: G15 — Pesticide handling and application task safety
purpose: Recognize product- and role-specific pesticide hazards and prevent exposure through suitable labeling, controls and handoff decisions.
practicalBoundary: Not EPA-approved WPS training, applicator certification, state-approved CE or a legal license. Product/method-specific approved training where required, jurisdiction/category qualification, practical assessment and employer authorization remain separate.

title: G21 — Nitrogen and inert-gas hazards: recognition, separation and safe handoff
purpose: Recognize nitrogen/oxygen-displacement, cryogenic and catalyst interfaces; prevent unprotected exposure and hand off to the qualified operating and emergency roles.
practicalBoundary: Knowledge foundation only. Actual nitrogen/pressure/cryogenic/catalyst operating methods, technical gas testing, respiratory use, inert entry and atmospheric rescue require their own qualified programs, supervised practical evaluation and employer/site authorization. This course certifies none of those roles and provides no universal operating or alarm limits.

title: G22 — Facility support, water hygiene and biological task safety
purpose: Address TG31 foundation knowledge by distinguishing actual facility/water/biological duties and preventing contamination through suitable systems, hygiene and handoff decisions.
practicalBoundary: Foundation only: not a licensed water/treatment operator, plumbing/backflow, clinical, laboratory, confined-space or specialist cleanup qualification. Actual exposure confirmation, system/product methods, appropriate practical assessment and jurisdiction-specific requirements remain separate.

title: G23 — OT/cyber operational safety: defensive work boundaries and safe change
purpose: Recognize when digital work can affect physical safeguards and preserve authorized, coordinated defensive behavior without claiming technical operation or engineering competence.
practicalBoundary: This defensive knowledge foundation qualifies no operator, OT administrator, cyber incident responder, recovery engineer, electrical technician or functional-safety engineer. It grants no permission to scan, probe, bypass controls, alter configuration, operate equipment, collect intrusive evidence, restore production or authorize restart. Actual system/task instruction, qualified technical and safe practical assessment, employer/site approval and any applicable credentials remain separate.
